requirement: Parse untrusted YAML configuration files using safe_load to prevent arbitrary Python code execution, verifying schema mappings and wrapping syntax errors.
skeleton: PipelineManifestParser class and parse_manifest helper with ConfigValidationError.
caption: A PyYAML manifest parser that treats configuration text as untrusted and never lets it construct Python objects. ConfigValidationError subclasses Exception. PipelineManifestParser takes a tuple of required keys defaulting to version, pipeline, and steps, and raises ValueError when that tuple is empty. parse_manifest(content) raises TypeError when the content is not a string and ConfigValidationError when it is empty or only whitespace. It parses with yaml.safe_load, which only builds plain mappings, lists, and scalars, and converts any yaml.YAMLError, including the constructor error produced by a python/object or python/name tag, into ConfigValidationError chained from the original. It then raises ConfigValidationError when the document root is not a mapping, so a scalar or list document is refused, and raises ConfigValidationError naming the first required key that is missing. On success it returns the parsed dictionary. The module-level parse_manifest(yaml_text) builds a parser with the default keys and delegates to it. The fixture asserts that a valid manifest yields version 2.0, pipeline deployment, and two steps, that the helper parses a second manifest, that documents carrying code-execution and object-instantiation tags are rejected with a syntax or constructor message instead of running anything, that a scalar root is rejected, that a manifest without steps names the missing key, that empty required keys are refused, and that empty or non-string content is rejected.

rationale.teaches: Parsing untrusted YAML with safe_load only, requiring a mapping root, checking every required key is present, and wrapping syntax errors.
rationale.why: yaml.load with the full or unsafe Loader parses every benign document identically and executes arbitrary Python on a crafted one. The fixture feeds a python/object tag and expects it to be rejected.

candidates.why_wrong: yaml.Loader is used, so a python/object tag in the manifest instantiates arbitrary classes.
A non-mapping root is accepted, so a scalar or list document passes as a manifest and breaks the next key lookup.
The key check is inverted, so a manifest with all required keys is rejected and one with none passes.
The empty required_keys guard compares a length to a negative number, so it never fires.
FullLoader is used, which still resolves python/name and other tags that safe_load refuses.
